title: The Holiday
tagline: Swap houses. Keep the cheese board.
about: Two heartbroken women swap homes for Christmas, one in Surrey and one in Los Angeles.
cue: Serve the snacks when Amanda opens the door of the snowy Surrey cottage.

    StartersSurrey cottage cheese boardAged cheddar, brie and blue cheese with oatcakes, quince paste, apple and walnutsHow to make it150g aged cheddar150g brie150g blue cheese1 packet oatcakes1 small tub quince paste1 apple100g walnutsBring the cheddar, brie and blue cheese to room temperature.Arrange the cheddar, brie and blue cheese on a wooden board with oatcakes, quince paste, sliced apple and walnuts.Set it by the fire with a glass of something warm.Rosehill Cottage Welsh rarebitToast under a melted alcohol-free beer and mustard cheddar sauceHow to make it20g butter1 tbsp plain flour80ml ginger beer200g vintage cheddar, grated1 tsp English mustard1 dash Worcestershire sauce6 slices of sourdoughMelt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then whisk in the ginger beer.Add the cheddar, mustard and Worcestershire and stir over low heat until thick and smooth.Toast the sourdough.Spread the cheese mixture thickly to the edges and grill until bubbling and browned in spots.Cut in half and serve hot.LA pool house green goddess cruditésAmanda's huge house in Los AngelesHow to make itAs written, serves 4Baby carrots, radishes, cucumber and snow peas on ice around a bright green goddess dip of avocado, herbs, lemon and Greek yoghurt.Blitz an avocado, 150g Greek yoghurt, a handful each of parsley, basil and chives, a garlic clove, 2 anchovies, the juice of a lemon and salt until smooth and green.Trim 2 bunches baby carrots and a bunch of radishes, cut a Lebanese cucumber into batons and trim 150g snow peas.Arrange the vegetables over a tray of crushed ice with the dip in the middle.Crumpets with honey butterGraham knocks late. Amanda opens the door.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsGraham's family pastaSpaghetti in a slow-simmered tomato and butter sauce with basil and parmesanHow to make it800g tins crushed tomatoes80g butter1 brown onion500g spaghetti1 small bunch basil100g parmesan, gratedsalt, to tastePeel and halve the onion.Simmer the tomatoes with butter and onion, stirring now and then.Remove the onion and season.Cook the spaghetti.Toss with the sauce and finish with torn basil and plenty of parmesan.Arthur's lemon thyme roast chickenIris throwing a dinner for Arthur and his old friendsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Whole chicken rubbed with lemon and thyme butter, roasted golden, with crisp roast potatoes, honey glazed carrots and gravy made from the pan.Mix 60g soft butter with lemon zest, chopped thyme and salt and push under the skin of a 1.8kg chicken.Put the halved lemon inside.Roast at 200°C for 75 minutes.Parboil 1kg potatoes, rough them up and roast in oil alongside for an hour.Glaze 500g carrots with butter and honey.Rest the chicken, then stir flour into the pan juices and whisk in 300ml stock for gravy.SweetsSticky toffee puddingWarm date the eggs, dates and flour.Bake at 180°C.Simmer the butter and brown sugar for the sauce with the cream into a toffee sauce.Poke holes in the pudding and pour over the hot sauce.Serve with ice
